name: Eliakim
title: Overseer in Jerusalem
summary: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, was the overseer in King Hezekiah's household in Judah. He played a central role during the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem and was described by the prophet Isaiah as God's chosen servant who would bear the key to the house of David. His position and the prophecy concerning him point forward to the authority of the Messiah.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Overseer
keyEvents.description: God declared through the prophet Isaiah that Eliakim would replace Shebna as overseer and have the key to the house of David placed on his shoulder.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Meet Rabshakeh
keyEvents.description: When the Assyrian commander Rabshakeh came to Jerusalem with threats, King Hezekiah sent Eliakim along with Shebna and Joah to negotiate with him.

keyEvents.title: Rabshakeh's Speech at the City Wall
keyEvents.description: Eliakim asked Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic instead of Hebrew so that the people on the wall would not understand the threats. Rabshakeh refused and spoke even louder.

keyEvents.title: Messenger to the Prophet Isaiah
keyEvents.description: After hearing Rabshakeh's threats, Eliakim and the others tore their clothes in mourning and went to the prophet Isaiah to seek God's word and guidance.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy about Eliakim as God's Servant
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesied that Eliakim would become like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the house of Judah, and that God would give him authority and honor like a peg driven into a firm place.

keyEvents.title: Typological Connection to Christ
keyEvents.description: The prophecy that the key of the house of David would be placed on Eliakim's shoulder was later referenced in Revelation concerning Christ, who holds the key of David and opens so that no one can shut.
